title: Rebalancing vs changing the target
objectives: Separate rebalancing from target changes on trigger, reason and frequency.
Name the never-reasons for changing a target.
body_md:
Rebalancing returns the portfolio to the same target. Changing the target is a different decision, and it needs its own reason and the client's agreement.

|  | Rebalancing | Changing the target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Triggered by | Market movement (drift) | Life or goal change |
| Examples | 60/40 drifted to 66/34; bring it back | Goal now 3 years away; move to 30/70 (glide path) |
| How often | Yearly check, or when a band is breached | Only when the client's situation changes |
| Valid reasons | Drift beyond the band | Goal date nearer, life event, new risk profile |
| Never because of | — | A market view, news, or last year's returns |
example: Goal now 3 years away; move to 30/70 (glide path) — that is a target change, not a rebalance, and needs the client's agreement.
say: Target change: never because of a market view, news, or last year's returns.
never: Change the target because markets look expensive.
Rebalance to 60/40 when the goal is 2 years away.

check.q: A goal is now 2 years away. The client asks to “rebalance to 60/40”. You…
o: Explain a new target (glide path) is needed
check.why: Explain a new target (glide path) is needed. That is a target change, not a rebalance.

check.q: Which is a valid reason to change the target?
check.why: A life event. Goal, life or risk-profile changes.

check.q: Is a market view a good reason to change the target mix?
o: Yes, if the view is strong
No — only goal, life or risk-profile changes justify it
check.why: Only goal, life or risk-profile changes justify it.
